q.intro.text: A roof frame: the brace D E runs parallel to the beam B C. A D is four feet, D B is six feet, and the brace D E is five feet. How long is the beam B C? Pick one, and say how sure you are.

q.cb.part.text: You paired A D with D B, the part below it. But the beam belongs to the big triangle, whose side is the whole of A B, ten feet. Four tenths of B C is five, so B C is twelve and a half feet.

q.cb.add.text: You added the extra six feet. Similar triangles grow by a factor, not by an amount: A B is ten fourths of A D, so B C is ten fourths of D E, twelve and a half feet.

q.cb.ok.text: You said twelve and a half feet, and the proof agrees: A D pairs with the whole side A B, and the part to part ratio only holds on the two cut sides.

e.intro.text: Why must the two triangles have the same shape? Watch the proof, then the dilation that carries one onto the other.

e.step0.text: Two angle pairs. Both triangles share angle A, by the reflexive property. The brace is parallel to the beam, so angle A D E matches angle A B C: corresponding angles. No side lengths are needed.

e.step1.text: Two angle pairs are enough for triangles: triangle A D E is similar to triangle A B C, by A A. The order matters: A with A, D with B, E with C.

e.step2.text: Why A A works: dilate the small triangle from A by k equals ten over four. D lands on B, the parallel brace lands on the beam, and E lands on C.

e.step3.text: Every side grows by the same factor, ten fourths. So A D over A B equals D E over B C: four tenths equals five over B C, and B C is twelve and a half feet.

e.why.text: Why does A D pair with A B, which is ten, and not with D B, which is six?

e.why.ok.text: Right: A B is the side of the big triangle that matches A D. D B is only part of it.

e.why.either.text: Not either: A D and D B are both on the line, but only A B is a side of the big triangle.

e.why.next.text: D B is next to the beam, but it is not a side of either triangle. Match a side of the small triangle with a side of the big one.

t.intro.text: Your turn: an hourglass. A B is parallel to C D, and A C and B D cross at E. A E is six, E C is nine, and A B is eight. First: which statement is justified?

t.a.ok.text: Right: vertical angles at E, and alternate interior angles at A and C. A matches C, B matches D, E matches E: a half turn about E, then a dilation.

t.a.pos.text: Not by position: the bottom triangle is turned upside down. A matches C through the alternate interior angles, not the vertex below it.

t.a.none.text: The arrow marks say A B is parallel to C D: that gives alternate interior angles as a second pair.

t.b.text: What is the scale factor from triangle A B E to triangle C D E?

t.b.ok.text: Right: E C over A E, nine over six, which is three halves. New over old.

t.b.flip.text: That is the factor the other way. From A B E to C D E: a side of C D E over its partner, nine over six.

t.b.add.text: That is a difference, nine minus six. A scale factor is a ratio: nine over six.

t.b.other.text: Use the pair you know in both triangles: E C matches A E, so k is nine over six.

t.c.ok.text: Right: C D is three halves of eight, which is twelve.

t.c.flip.text: That multiplies by two thirds. Triangle C D E is the bigger one: multiply A B by three halves.

t.c.add.text: That adds three. Similar sides are multiplied by one factor: eight times three halves.

t.c.other.text: C D matches A B, because A goes with C and B goes with D. Multiply eight by three halves.

t.done.text: One more idea is hiding in the first figure: the parallel cuts both sides in the same ratio. Time to prove it.

p.intro.text: Back to the roof frame, with A E four point eight feet and E C seven point two feet. The claim: a segment parallel to one side cuts the other two sides in the same ratio. A D over D B equals A E over E C. Always, or only for these numbers?

p.build.text: Build the proof: tap the reason for each line.

p.build-test.text: Checking numbers shows it here, not always. Build the general proof: tap the reason for each line.

p.claim1.text: Triangle A D E is similar to triangle A B C, with scale factor k, A B over A D.

p.claim2.text: A B is k times A D, and A C is k times A E, with the same k.

p.claim3.text: D B is k minus one times A D, and E C is k minus one times A E.

p.c1.text: A A: the shared angle and the corresponding angles.

p.c2.text: One scale factor for every pair of corresponding sides.

p.c3.text: Whole minus part, on both sides. So A D over D B equals A E over E C, both one over k minus one, for every parallel, not just these numbers.

p.x-part.text: D B and E C are parts, not sides of either triangle: they are not corresponding sides.

p.x-look.text: Looking cut at the same place is not a reason: the proof must work for every parallel.

p.x-other.text: That reason does not fit this line yet.

p.last.text: Does the side splitter also give A D over D B equals D E over B C?

p.last.ok.text: Right: D E and B C are not cut. They pair with whole sides: D E over B C equals A D over A B.

p.last.no.text: D E and B C are not cut by anything: only the two cut sides have part to part ratios. D E over B C equals A D over A B.
